units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 3. Code-design philosophy > Non-negotiables (enforced culturally + by CI budgets)
units.does: Claims enforced rules: functions 5-15 lines target/20 yellow; try? capped by .ci/try_optional_budget.txt (exists, value 170, enforced by enforce_tech_debt_budgets.sh); no magic numbers in logic — all thresholds centralized in Constants.swift (+Constants+RecoveryScore.swift); RRCollector.makeDefault() is the production composition root.

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 3. Code-design philosophy > Conventions you will see everywhere (so you can pattern-match)

FeatureFlags is actually declared in Constants+SleepAndDisplay.swift:422 (a final class, not an enum in Constants.swift).

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 3. Code-design philosophy > What NOT to do
units.does: Lists forbidden practices (sweeping rewrites, new global state, new magic numbers) and points to the REFACTOR_SPEC completion checklist, stating CI measures only part of it: check_refactor_spec_conformance.sh covers function/property/init length, nesting depth, commented-out code and empty catches, other gates own try?, .shared and log redaction; magic numbers (no_magic_numbers is not enabled in either SwiftLint config) and the judgement items are held by review only.

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 7. End-to-end flows > 7.1 App launch & navigation
units.does: Claims launch: EmuquApp creates collector (RRCollector.makeDefault) + five sub-objects, syncManager, settingsManager, storeKitManager, languageManager, voiceChat, watchBridge, emailBridge as @State and injects them via .environment; heavy setup deferred to boot() via runDeferredBoot(); 8 s safety timeout; launch gating via LaunchModal presented with fullScreenCover in loadDataAndContinue() in order disclaimer → onboarding → paywall → trial reminder → score-architecture change → else interrupted-session check; per-tab NavigationStack reset by MainTabView.resetPath(from:to:). Verified: runDeferredBoot boots watchBridge/collector/syncManager/storeKitManager/voiceChat (AppLaunchTasks.swift:141-149); 8_000_000_000 ns timer (AppLaunchTasks.swift:183); environment injection EmuquApp.swift:310-321,333.

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 7. End-to-end flows > 7.2 Overnight recording → recovery score → dashboard
units.does: Claims overnight spine: RRCollector.startOvernightStreaming arms H10 internal recording as backup (never on Verity Sense), ~60 s incremental raw-RR backup; StrapLinkCoordinator gives PolarReconnectPolicy.windowSeconds (20 min) before reconnectExhausted; Stop = RecordView.stopOvernightAndApplyOutcome -> RRCollector.stopOvernightStreaming -> OvernightStreamingCoordinator.stopOvernightStreaming (end arming, stop streaming infrastructure, back up beats, download/merge/score with bounded reconnect and parallel sleep poll, fallbackToDeviceFetch for a short stream); gatherOvernightData named as the pause/recovery gather; DataSourceSelector.selectBestSource internal → composite → streaming → raw backup, composite gap threshold 2 s; HRVAnalysisPipeline.analyzeWithAutoWindow runs WindowSelector.findBestWindow over 30-70% of sleep then analyzeWithWindow; computeRecoveryScore → calculateWithBreakdown 0-100 HRV60/Sleep25/Vitals15 stored 0-10 via toTenScale; archive + archiveSignal.notifyChanged + CloudKit upload; MainTabView.startDashboardLoad reloads recentSessionsAsync(limit: 35).

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 7. End-to-end flows > 7.3 Workout recording → summary
units.does: Claims workout flow: WorkoutRecorder reconnects strap/Stryd/FTMS/PM5, starts GPS and barometric buffer; LiveDFAAnalyzer rolling α1 every 20 s; LiveWorkoutBroker snapshot; WorkoutTriggerEngine + WorkoutVoiceCoach; stopStreaming deferred until a 120 s HRR window (HRRCaptureService captureWindowSec = 120, HRRCaptureService.swift:27); finalizeSession runs WorkoutAnalyzer (TRIMP, hrTSS, power-TSS, splits, decoupling), elevation post-processing, archives and auto-archives a breadcrumb; WorkoutPDFReport.generate produces the PDF. The 20 s cadence matches an init default `cadenceSec: TimeInterval = 20` with 120 s window (LiveDFAAnalyzer).

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 7. End-to-end flows > 7.4 An AI turn (Flo)
units.does: Claims an AI turn: AssistantViewModel.send → DeterministicIntent.tryMatch zero-token shortcut → dispatch → resolveProviderForThisTurn (pure core TurnRouter) with RoutingMode active only while Apple is selected; Auto → CapabilityClassifier → SmartProviderRouter tier; TierProviderMapper mid tier Grok then DeepSeek else Apple (TierProviderMapper.swift:168); 50/day cap on deep turns (dailyTier3Cap = 50, SmartProviderRouter.swift:48); runToolUseLoop with CompactToolRouter.resolveTool and maxToolCallsPerTurn = 8 (AssistantViewModel+Tools.swift:30); Apple path compacts at 70% of 4096 (AppleContextCompactor.swift:43,48), SessionCache rotates after 20 turns (maxTurnsPerSession = 20), 512-token replies (responseReserve = 512). The '~15 deterministic queries' and prewarm-on-first-send claims were not traced.

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 7. End-to-end flows > 7.5 Storage & iCloud sync
units.does: Claims storage/sync: SessionArchive.archive writes JSON to the App Group, stores SHA-256, updates the locked index, persists it; CloudKitSyncManager.uploadSession only when sync is on strips Health-sourced fields via CloudSessionPayload.uploadable (sleep/vitals snapshots, sleep window, training/analysis/breakdown Health readings, Watch HR) then ZLIB-compresses and encrypts into a private-DB CKAsset; performFullSync on launch/foreground; soft-delete isDeleted and deletedSessionIds; runDeferredMigrations runs one-time migrations in the background. uploadable verified CloudKitSyncSupport.swift:564-581; isDeleted tombstones CloudKitSyncManager+Deletion.swift:163-198.

units.key: § Emuqu — Maintainer's Guide > 10. Build, test, CI & tooling > The code map
units.does: Describes docs/codemap/records (a record per Swift function, initializer, computed property, protocol requirement, script function, Makefile target, workflow step and Markdown section, with what it does, triggers, calls, shared state and branches); the call graph (recorded calls plus calls, property reads, protocol dispatch and closure assignments found in the code); make codemap-impact (callers up to triggers, tests, docs, shared state and its other users; the same list in the gates.yml PR job summary); and make codemap-guard (in make ci, both workflows and the pre-commit hook) failing on a missing or empty record or code changed since stamping, and counting the re-check lines (callee now describes different behaviour, a new certain callee, or a record naming a unit that no longer exists), which codemap.py status lists. Gives the change procedure (impact, change, rewrite, re-check, stamp callees first) with links to codemap/README.md and CLAUDE.md, and states the limits: the guard proves timing, not correctness; without a type checker ambiguous names are possible callers and only certain edges trigger re-checks. Every claim matches codemap.py, graph.py and the workflows.
